commit_message:
lavf/mxfdec: Speed up mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset()

This involves computing the approximate location of the desired index table segment and linearly searching from there.
pr_description: This involves computing the approximate location of the desired index table segment and linearly searching from there.

fix_commit.message: avformat/mxfdec: Check edit_unit for being larger than signed 64bit
fix_commit.author: Michael Niedermayer

findings.title: Missing negative-value check on clamped edit_unit allows signed 64-bit overflow
findings.message: In mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset(), after edit_unit is rescaled via av_rescale_q() it is clamped with `edit_unit = FFMAX(FFMIN(edit_unit, index_end), first_segment->index_start_position);`. This clamp does not guarantee edit_unit is non-negative: if first_segment->index_start_position itself is a huge negative value (attacker-controlled via a crafted MXF index table segment), edit_unit can remain an extremely large negative int64 value (e.g. close to INT64_MIN). This value then flows into the segment-search loop where `int64_t index = edit_unit - s->index_start_position;` is computed and, for VBR/Avid indexes, `index *= 2;` is executed when `s->nb_index_entries == 2 * s->index_duration + 1`. Multiplying a value close to INT64_MIN by 2 causes signed integer overflow (undefined behavior), as reported by UBSan fuzzing ('signed integer overflow: 2 * -4962931467012268000 cannot be represented in type long'). The function lacks a check that edit_unit remains within a sane, non-negative range after clamping before it is used in further arithmetic.
findings.suggestion: After clamping edit_unit to the index range, explicitly reject negative values before using edit_unit in further arithmetic (index computation, doubling for Avid indexes, etc.), since a crafted MXF file can make first_segment->index_start_position an extremely large negative number that survives the FFMAX/FFMIN clamp.

ground_truth.root_cause: The refactored fast-path clamp added in the 'Speed up mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset()' commit clamps edit_unit's upper and lower bound using index metadata read directly from the file, without validating the sign/range of the resulting edit_unit before it is used in subsequent signed integer arithmetic (including a multiplication by 2 for Avid-style indexes).

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Missing negative-value check on clamped edit_unit allows signed 64-bit overflow
